Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise design-input card for a bounded Expansion Assist proposal before design work begins. Capture the key observed pilot pattern and the evidence limitations that reviewers must preserve. Title it `Expansion Assist — bounded proposal evidence card`.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Expansion Assist — bounded proposal evidence card", "folder": "Growth", "body": "As of January 1, 2028

Purpose
Design input for a bounded Expansion Assist proposal. This is not launch, rollout, or Sales-queue approval.

Observed pilot pattern
- Across two bounded pilots with closed, complete 45-day windows: 43 actual exposures, 13 help-or-options requests, and 9 expansions.
- The pattern is directional: behavior-based signals can identify retained mid-segment accounts that may ask for help/options and may later expand.
- The useful design learning is the state-and-handoff model: recent active-admin behavior, meaningful integration depth, and product-visible usage-ceiling evidence must be interpreted together; open Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses commercial prompting and keeps the account CS-first.
- Keep exposure, help/technical interaction, commercial request, handoff, and qualifying expansion outcome as separate measures.

Evidence limits reviewers must preserve
- Descriptive only: there was no randomized control or explicit comparison, so the results do not establish causal lift or attribution.
- Do not treat the counts as a forecast, revenue commitment, pipeline source, or proof of broad retained-mid readiness.
- The usage-ceiling recency rule was applied only to the second cohort; 18 of the first pilot’s 30 exposures had an older ceiling event. Do not present the cohorts as methodologically identical.
- Do not infer readiness from seat count, usage-ceiling evidence alone, deep integration alone, stale expansion quotes, or retained-mid status.
- Preserve suppression, state-specific eligibility, normal commercial qualification, and Customer Success ownership of the live handling path.
- Keep Expansion Assist separate from Helio Start and from any other motion’s activation or revenue evidence.

Design gate
Before any live proposal: document eligibility, exposure and handoff states, suppression logic, denominators, guardrails, and an explicit comparison plan if causal claims are contemplated."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_059_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document accurately states the observed concentration: all six expansions and seven of the eight help requests came from the 12 exposed accounts whose product-visible usage ceiling had been crossed within the preceding 14 days. It may also note that the other 18 exposed accounts produced one help request and no expansions. Missing or materially contradicting the concentration must fail.

The document explicitly limits interpretation of the pilot: the result is descriptive or observational, does not establish causal lift, and does not justify a broad rollout. Missing either the non-causal limitation or the no-broad-rollout boundary must fail.", "value": {"title": "Expansion Assist — bounded proposal evidence card", "folder": "Growth", "body": "As of January 1, 2028

- The pattern is directional: behavior-based signals can identify retained mid-segment accounts that may ask for help/options and may later expand.
- The useful design learning is the state-and-handoff model: recent active-admin behavior, meaningful integration depth, and product-visible usage-ceiling evidence must be interpreted together; open Customer Success adoption or renewal work suppresses commercial prompting and keeps the account CS-first.
- Keep exposure, help/technical interaction, commercial request, handoff, and qualifying expansion outcome as separate measures.

Evidence limits reviewers must preserve
- Descriptive only: there was no randomized control or explicit comparison, so the results do not establish causal lift or attribution.
- Do not treat the counts as a forecast, revenue commitment, pipeline source, or proof of broad retained-mid readiness.
- The usage-ceiling recency rule was applied only to the second cohort; 18 of the first pilot’s 30 exposures had an older ceiling event. Do not present the cohorts as methodologically identical.
- Do not infer readiness from seat count, usage-ceiling evidence alone, deep integration alone, stale expansion quotes, or retained-mid status.
